name: run

name: stop

returns: T for veto-capable captured/current close or notify events; NIL otherwise.
description: Snapshots read copied capability without a session. Current close contexts use CanVeto; current notify contexts always support Veto/Allow. Plain command contexts return NIL. Scope validation remains required for native access. Context SETF maps native SetCanVeto directly, including false to true. GetVeto hides a stored veto when CanVeto is false and reveals it again if re-enabled. Forced close starts false but explicit metadata mutation can affect native closing results; OS veto acceptance is not guaranteed.
scope: Active main-thread session required for native context or frame operations. Expired/suspended contexts and invalid/deleting frames signal NATIVE-ERROR. Saved snapshots need no session. Close and registered notify families permit checked veto. Native control-specific notify subclasses, validated OS session delivery and arbitrary event classes remain open.
wxwidgets: wxCloseEvent::CanVeto / SetCanVeto; intrinsic wxNotifyEvent capability is read-only (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

setf.description: Assign current wxCloseEvent capability, returning VALUE. Snapshot, command and notify writers reject; stale/suspended contexts reject native access. Does not clear the native stored veto bit or guarantee OS policy.

name: event-vetoed-p
arguments: EVENT is a saved snapshot or current close/notify context. SETF requires a current veto-capable context.
returns: Copied/current veto state as T/NIL; SETF returns the supplied generalized boolean.
description: Snapshots retain pre-callback state. Close contexts use GetVeto / checked Veto(bool); notify contexts use NOT IsAllowed, Veto() for true, and Allow() for NIL. A close initialized non-vetoable rejects writes unless its current CanVeto flag was explicitly enabled through SETF EVENT-CAN-VETO-P. Plain command contexts reject live veto-state access. Snapshots stay immutable. Native GetVeto is CanVeto AND the stored veto bit; disabling capability hides the bit without clearing it.
scope: Active main-thread session required for native context or frame operations. Expired/suspended contexts and invalid/deleting frames signal NATIVE-ERROR. Saved snapshots need no session. Close and registered notify families permit checked veto. Native control-specific notify subclasses, validated OS session delivery and arbitrary event classes remain open.
wxwidgets: wxCloseEvent::GetVeto / Veto(bool); wxNotifyEvent::IsAllowed / Veto / Allow. (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

setf.description: Close contexts require CanVeto true before either assignment. Notify true invokes Veto and NIL invokes Allow. Plain command contexts and stale/suspended contexts reject access; snapshots have no SETF method.

name: close-window
arguments: FRAME is a live FRAME. Optional FORCE defaults NIL; true initializes native CanVeto false.
returns: Native close acceptance as T/NIL; not a destruction/liveness guarantee.
description: Synchronously generate the frame close request via wxWindow::Close(force). A vetoed request returns NIL. A consuming contextual callback may return acceptance T without deleting anything, even for FORCE. Set Skip true to delegate to native default closing when appropriate. Callback conditions re-signal at this Lisp boundary; a handled nested condition does not stop RUN. Use DESTROY-WINDOW for explicit destruction. A callback can explicitly mutate CanVeto through SETF EVENT-CAN-VETO-P; FORCE is not an immutable capability limit.
scope: Active main-thread session required for native context or frame operations. Expired/suspended contexts and invalid/deleting frames signal NATIVE-ERROR. Saved snapshots need no session. Close and registered notify families permit checked veto. Native control-specific notify subclasses, validated OS session delivery and arbitrary event classes remain open.

name: register-event-type
arguments: NAME is a unique keyword not reserved by a built-in kind. FAMILY is :NOTIFY (default) or :COMMAND.
returns: The supplied NAME keyword.
description: Allocate a process-local native event type and map NAME in the active session. Duplicate names, built-ins and unsupported families are rejected before registration. Names cannot be unregistered or replaced during this session. Registrations are session-wide metadata, not rolled back when an unrelated resource initializer fails. Native type IDs are not stable across processes.
scope: Active main-thread session required for registration/dispatch and scoped native access; inactive calls signal NATIVE-ERROR before FFI. Wrong receiver types use CLOS dispatch errors. Registry metadata lasts until session cleanup; snapshot data is immutable. Borrowed application dispatch is supported; no worker dispatch, validated OS session delivery or arbitrary native class construction is provided.
wxwidgets: wxNewEventType; synthetic wxCommandEvent/wxNotifyEvent family registration (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: process-event
arguments: HANDLER is a live EVENT-HANDLER/window. KIND and keyword payloads match QUEUE-EVENT. LOGGING-OFF-P defaults NIL and is accepted only for :QUERY-END-SESSION/:END-SESSION; CAN-VETO-P applies to all close-family kinds.
returns: Two values: native handled-p and final vetoed-p.
description: Synchronously dispatch a fresh owned synthetic event through ProcessEvent, copy final veto state and then delete the event. Observer callbacks may run while handled-p is NIL because they Skip; native consumption/default handling determines the first result. Final veto is independent of handled-p and may be true from initial VETOED-P even without a matching handler. Close dispatch can run frame defaults. Callback errors re-signal at the nearer Lisp boundary; handled nested errors do not stop RUN. No final values are returned when a condition escapes, and earlier callback mutations are not rolled back.
scope: Active main-thread session required for registration/dispatch and scoped native access; inactive calls signal NATIVE-ERROR before FFI. Wrong receiver types use CLOS dispatch errors. Registry metadata lasts until session cleanup; snapshot data is immutable. Borrowed application dispatch is supported; no worker dispatch, validated OS session delivery or arbitrary native class construction is provided. Synthetic session kinds require isolated owned standalone handlers; application/window receivers reject before emission. Standalone session fallback to wxApp is suppressed even for skipped, disabled or unmatched delivery. Native application session bindings are distinct from synthetic probes.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::ProcessEvent; wxCloseEvent::GetVeto or NOT wxNotifyEvent::IsAllowed after dispatch. (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: event-integer
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot.
returns: The copied signed native command integer; zero for close snapshots.
description: Read GetInt metadata for command/notify snapshots after callback/source/session cleanup. Registered event types accept an INTEGER payload; built-in toggle/selection events retain their specialized accessors. No mutable native integer setter or userData pointer is exposed.
scope: No active native session required for saved snapshots. Wrong argument types signal Lisp type errors.
wxwidgets: wxCommandEvent::GetInt copied into a Lisp-owned snapshot. (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: application-handler
arguments: No public constructor; obtain the session view with CURRENT-APPLICATION-HANDLER.
returns: An EVENT-HANDLER subclass representing the managed wxApp.
description: Borrowed native identity with inherited binding, dispatch, liveness and enabled state. Direct construction and subclass construction are rejected; explicit destruction signals NATIVE-ERROR. Session cleanup owns the native wxApp.
scope: One cached view in the active main-thread session. No native wxApp subclassing, replacement or ownership transfer; native session bindings exist but OS delivery remains unverified. Saved views reject native access outside the session.
wxwidgets: wxApp / wxAppConsole::GetInstance and wxTheApp, managed instance only (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

construction.description: Obtain the cached borrowed application view. Direct MAKE-INSTANCE, subclass construction and MAKE-EVENT-HANDLER construction are forbidden; only session cleanup owns native wxApp destruction.

name: current-application-handler
arguments: None.
returns: The EQ-identical APPLICATION-HANDLER view for the current session.
description: Borrow the bridge application event handler without constructing or taking ownership of wxApp. Native main-thread/session validation runs on every lookup, including cached lookups.
scope: Active main-thread session required; otherwise NATIVE-ERROR. One session per process. No external application adoption; native session bindings exist but OS delivery remains unverified.
wxwidgets: wxAppConsole::GetInstance / wxTheApp, bridge-managed application only (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: event-logging-off-p
arguments: EVENT is a saved session-event snapshot or current innermost session-event context. SETF VALUE is a generalized boolean.
returns: T for logging off, NIL for system shutdown; SETF returns VALUE.
description: Read copied or current wxCloseEvent logging-off metadata for :QUERY-END-SESSION/:END-SESSION. Context SETF changes native metadata only, not OS policy. Snapshots retain pre-callback state and have no SETF method.
scope: Saved session snapshots require no session. Non-session snapshots signal Lisp errors; non-session, stale or suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. Native access requires an active main-thread session. OS session delivery is not validated by isolated synthetic tests.

setf.description: Assign the current native session flag, returning the generalized boolean. No snapshot writer; no OS logout/shutdown action is performed.

name: event-timestamp
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot or current event context. SETF VALUE must fit signed native C long.
returns: Native millisecond timestamp as a Lisp integer; SETF returns VALUE.
description: Read copied/current native timestamp, not necessarily Unix time. Negative values including -1 are valid. Synthetic events start at zero. Context SETF changes metadata only, not scheduling. Snapshots stay immutable and preserve pre-callback values.
scope: Saved snapshot reads need no native session. Context access requires an active main-thread session and the innermost callback; expired/suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. Malformed/out-of-range SETF values signal TYPE-ERROR. Native LONG width is platform-specific; mouse/key events are not yet bound.
wxwidgets: wxEvent::GetTimestamp / SetTimestamp, native signed long widened to int64_t at the ABI (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

setf.description: Assign a signed native LONG timestamp to the current event. No snapshot writer or synthetic-constructor timestamp keyword. No Unix-epoch or scheduling meaning is implied.

name: event-command-p
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot or current event context.
returns: T for native command/notify-derived events; NIL for close-family events.
description: Read captured/current native IsCommandEvent classification. No mutable classification or event replacement. Saved values remain independent of source lifetime.
scope: Saved snapshots need no session. Current-context access requires an active main-thread session and the innermost callback; stale/suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. No SETF writer.

name: event-origin-id
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot or current innermost event context.
returns: Positive opaque bridge identity, or NIL for null/untracked native origin.
description: Copy/read GetEventObject identity only when it matches a registered application, owned handler or tracked window. This differs from EVENT-SOURCE (binding receiver) and EVENT-ID (routing metadata). Pointer identity is compared without dereferencing the origin; no native pointer or wrapper reconstruction is exposed.
scope: Saved values need no native session and imply no current liveness. Context reads require active main-thread session and innermost callback; expired/suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. Null and untracked origins both map to NIL. Registry lookup is at capture/read time, not a historical pointer-lifetime guarantee. No SETF writer, generic wxObject wrapper, origin retention or native ownership transfer.
